summary: Earth Detectives is an interactive web platform that turns NASA climate data into a map anyone can explore. Users can search for any of Colombia's 33 departments, move through the years and see how air and sea temperature have changed since 1981, using NASA POWER (MERRA-2), NASA GISTEMP and NOAA ERSSTv5 data. The platform compares years and regions, generates a main finding from the data, and tests every trend with linear regression and the Mann-Kendall test, explaining the result in plain language. Users can also upload their own CSV files from NASA Giovanni to analyze trends. Climate data is public but hard to use for students, teachers and local communities; our tool makes it understandable at the regional level. Our analysis shows that between 1981 and 2025, 32 of 33 departments got warmer, by 0.71 °C on average. The platform works on computers and phones, in English and Spanish.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Earth Detectives is a map-first web platform to explore temperature trends in Colombia. It opens on a satellite globe focused on Colombia that zooms down to a street-level satellite map, with the data layers visible at every zoom level.

Main features:

- Search for any of Colombia's 33 departments; the map moves to it and shows its profile: current temperature, difference from normal, warming rate per decade and change since the 1980s.

- Layers for sea surface temperature, air temperature by department, anomaly and trend.

- Timeline to move through the years, with climate events such as El Niño and La Niña.

- Comparison between two years (each department colored by how much it warmed or cooled) and between 2 to 4 regions, with a summary box and a main finding calculated from the data.

- Interactive charts with exact values, period selection, zoom and line/bar views.

- Upload of user CSV files (for example from NASA Giovanni), with validation, data summary and trend analysis.

HOW IT WORKS

Air temperature by department is the average of the NASA POWER (MERRA-2) cells inside each department, from 1981 to 2025. Trends are calculated with linear regression and the Mann-Kendall test; a trend is reported as clear only when both tests give p < 0.05. Results are explained in plain language, with the technical details available but collapsed. When a source has no data for a year or region, the platform says so instead of estimating.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Climate data is public but difficult to use without technical training. Our platform lets students, teachers, local authorities and the general public see what NASA data says about their own region. Our analysis found that 32 of 33 departments warmed between 1981 and 2025, by 0.71 °C on average, with the largest increases in Norte de Santander and Vichada (above 1.2 °C).

TOOLS

JavaScript, HTML and CSS; d3.js for the globe and charts; WebGL2 for the satellite globe; Leaflet for the street map; Node.js and Express for the server and API; deployed on Render; code on GitHub.

CREATIVITY AND DESIGN DECISIONS

We focused on making statistics understandable: every view starts with a short answer, then the numbers, then the technical detail. The map is always the main element, the interface uses little text, it works on phones with pinch-to-zoom, and it is available in English and Spanish.
